# Part 1 · Identifiers

Every merge needs a **key**: one or more variables that identify an observation uniquely.
In accounting research, the most important keys are:

| Identifier | Identifies | Source | Watch out |
|-------------------|-------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `gvkey` | a firm | Compustat | 6-digit **text** with leading zeros |
| `permno` | a security (share class) | CRSP | a firm can have several permnos |
| `cusip` | a security | US/Canada | changes after name changes |
| `ticker` | a security | exchanges | **reused** after delistings |
| `isin` | a security | international | 12 characters, starts with a country code |
| company name | — | everywhere | spelling varies: "BMW" vs. "Bayerische Motoren Werke AG" |

A key for **firm-year data** is usually a combination, e.g. `gvkey` + `fyear`.

### Chunk 1.1 · Why names are bad keys

```{r chunk_1_1}
## Join by name: how many matches?

reports <- tibble(company = c("BMW", "Siemens Energy", "SAP"),
                  year = 2024,
                  scope1 = c(1.1, 0.3, 0.02))
database <- tibble(company = c("Bayerische Motoren Werke AG", "Siemens Energy AG", "SAP SE"),
                   year = 2024,
                   revenue = c(142380, 34465, 34176))

left_join(reports, database, by = c("company","year"))
```

*Illustrative numbers.* Not a single match — although all three firms are in both tables.
That is why we use codes such as `isin` or `gvkey`, and why name matching ("fuzzy matching") is a last resort that must be checked by hand.

### Chunk 1.2 · What does a valid ISIN look like?

An ISIN has 12 characters: a 2-letter country code, 9 alphanumeric characters and a check digit, e.g.
`DE0005190003` (BMW).

```{r chunk_1_2}

isins <- c("DE0005190003", "de0005190003", "DE000519000", " DE0005190003", NA)
nchar(isins)

str_detect(isins, "^[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{9}[0-9]$")

str_sub(isins, 1, 2)

## Repair what can be repaired: trim spaces, upper case
isins_clean <- str_to_upper(str_trim(isins))
isins_clean
```

**Lesson:** before you merge, check that keys look the way they should.
A lower-case letter or an invisible space is enough to break a merge — without any error message.

# Part 2 · Getting data from an API: the SRN database

The **Sustainability Reporting Navigator (SRN)** collects data from European sustainability reports (ESRS).
Its *Main ESRS KPI* dataset contains 27 indicators (emissions, energy, employees, revenues, …) for more than 600 firms, partly extracted by humans and partly by AI.

An **API** (application programming interface) lets your code ask a server for data:

1.  You send a **request** to a URL (an *endpoint*), often with a **token** that says who you are.
2.  The server sends a **response**: a status code (200 = OK, 401 = not authorised, 404 = not found) and the data, usually as JSON or CSV.

Advantages over clicking "download": the download becomes part of your code, so it is **documented and reproducible** — and you can pin an exact version of the data.

### Chunk 2.1 · An open endpoint: release metadata (no token needed)

```{r api_2_1}

base_url <- "https://api.srnav.com"

meta <- request(base_url) |> 
  req_url_path_append("projects", "main-esrs-kpi", "releases", "v2.4", "meta") |> 
  req_perform() |> 
  resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)

names(meta)
meta$version
meta$row_count

srn_companies <- as_tibble(meta$companies)
srn_fields <- as_tibble(meta$fields)

## Save a raw copy: raw data is never edited
write_csv(srn_companies |>  mutate(stock_index = map_chr(stock_index, ~paste(.x, collapse = ";"))),
          here("data", "srn_companies_v2.4.csv"))

write_csv(srn_fields, here("data", "srn_fields_v2.4.csv"))

srn_companies <- read_csv(here("data", "srn_companies_v2.4.csv"), trim_ws = FALSE) # keep spaces as they are
srn_fields <- read_csv(here("data","srn_fields_v2.4.csv"))

```

\

```{r chunk_2_1b}


```

### Chunk 2.2 · Your API token: keep it secret

The data values need a personal token.
Create one at **srnav.com → MySRN → API** (`srnav.com/dashboard/api`).

**Never** write the token into your R Markdown — it would end up on GitHub.
Store it in your personal `.Renviron` file instead:

```{r chunk_2_2, eval=FALSE}
## Run ONCE in the Console. A file opens: add the line
##   SRN_TOKEN=srn_your_token_here
## save it, then restart R (Session -> Restart R).
#usethis::edit_r_environ()

## Check (shows TRUE, not the token itself)
nchar(Sys.getenv("SRN_TOKEN")) > 0
```

### Chunk 2.3 · Download the data values (pinned to release v2.4)

```{r api_2_3}

resp <- request(base_url) |> 
  req_url_path_append("projects", "main-esrs-kpi","releases","v2.4.csv") |> 
  req_auth_bearer_token(Sys.getenv("SRN_TOKEN")) |> 
  req_perform()

resp_status(resp)

## Save the raw download unchanged

writeBin(resp_body_raw(resp), here("data", "srn_main_esrs_kpi_v2.4.csv"))


```

**Why `v2.4` and not `latest`?** `latest` changes whenever SRN publishes a new release.
Your results would change without you noticing.
Pinning the version makes your analysis reproducible.

### Chunk 2.4 · Read and inspect the raw data

```{r chunk_2_4}

srn_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "srn_main_esrs_kpi_v2.4.csv"),
                    col_types = cols(.default =col_character()))

dim(srn_raw)

names(srn_raw)

head(srn_raw)

## One row per ... ?
srn_raw |>  count(field_slug) |> print(n=30)

n_distinct(srn_raw$company_id)
table(srn_raw$year, useNA = "ifany")

## The value column: numbers as text — and a special code
srn_raw |>  filter(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value)))) |>  count(value, sort = TRUE)

```

The data are in **long format**: one row per company × year × indicator.
For analysis we usually want **wide format**: one row per company-year, one column per indicator (Chunk 3.4).

# Part 3 · Missing values and duplicates

## Missing values

A missing value (`NA`) can mean very different things:

- the firm **did not report** the indicator (e.g. no Scope 3 emissions),
- the indicator **does not apply** (e.g. no land use for a software firm),
- the value **was not extracted** (yet) — a data problem, not a firm decision.

These are different economic stories.
Treating all of them as "zero" or simply dropping them can bias your results.

### Chunk 3.1 · How much is missing?

```{r chunk_3_1}
## Missing per variable
## Three kinds of "missing" in the SRN data:
##   (1) value is NA, (2) value is the code "NOT_FOUND", (3) the row does not exist at all


srn_raw |>
  group_by(field_slug) |> 
  summarise(rows = n(),
            na = sum(is.na(value)),
            not_found = sum(value == "NOT_FOUND", na.rm = TRUE),
            share_found = mean(!is.na(value) & value != "NOT_FOUND")) |> 
  arrange(share_found) |> 
  print(n = 30)
                     
                      
## (3) Missing rows: how many company-years should there be?
n_company_years <- srn_raw |> distinct(company_id, year) |> nrow()
  
n_company_years # each indicator should have this many rows


```

### Chunk 3.2 · Text that looks fine but is not

```{r chunk_3_2}
## Countries: spot the problem
srn_companies |>  count(country) |>  print(n=30)

## Invisible trailing spaces
srn_companies |> filter(country != str_trim(country)) |> select(name, country)

## Firms without ISIN: what do their IDs look like?
srn_companies |>  filter(is.na(isin)) |> select(id, name, country)

## Does the ISIN country prefix match the country? (not always — and that can be fine)
srn_companies |> 
  filter(!is.na(isin)) |> 
  mutate(isin_prefix = str_sub(isin, 1, 2)) |> 
  count(country, isin_prefix) |> 
  arrange(country, desc(n))


```

## Duplicates

Before you merge or reshape, check that your key is unique: **one row per key**.
If not, find out *why* before you decide what to do.

### Chunk 3.3 · Is the key unique?

```{r chunk_3_3}
## SRN: key = company_id + year + field_slug
srn_raw |> 
  count(company_id, year, field_slug) |> 
  filter(n > 1)


## Compustat (Tutorial 1): key = gvkey + fyear?
cs <- read_csv(here("data", "compustat.csv"),
               col_types = cols(gvkey = col_character()), guess_max = Inf)

cs |> count(gvkey, fyear) |>  filter(n > 1) |> head()
## Why? Look at one duplicate
cs |>  filter(gvkey == "001062") |> select(gvkey, fyear, indfmt, conm, at, sale)


```

The Compustat duplicates are the same firm-year in two **formats**: `INDL` (industrial) and `FS` (financial services).
The standard solution is to keep `indfmt == "INDL"`.

```{r chunk_3_3b}

cs_indl <- cs |> filter(indfmt == "INDL", !is.na(fyear))
cs_indl |>  count(gvkey, fyear) |>  filter(n>1) |>  nrow() 


## Who is left?
cs_indl |> 
  add_count(gvkey, fyear) |> 
  filter(n > 1) |> 
  select(gvkey, fyear, datadate, conm, at, sale)

```

One firm reports **two fiscal year-ends per year** — it changed its fiscal year (June → December) and Compustat keeps both.
A rule we can defend: keep the later `datadate` per firm-year.

```{r chunk_3_3c}

cs_indl <- cs_indl |> 
  arrange(gvkey, fyear, desc(datadate)) |> 
  distinct(gvkey, fyear, .keep_all = TRUE)

cs_indl |> count(gvkey, fyear) |> filter(n > 1) |>  nrow() 


```

### Chunk 3.4 · From long to wide

```{r chunk_3_4}

srn_wide <- srn_raw |> 
  select(company_id, isin, company_name, country, year, field_slug, value) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = field_slug, values_from = value)

## Values are text. Convert the numeric indicators:
num_fields <- srn_fields |>  filter(data_type %in% c("number", "percentage")) |> pull(slug)


srn_wide <- srn_wide |> 
  mutate(country = str_trim(country),
         across(any_of(num_fields), ~ parse_number(.x, na = c("", "NA", "NOT_FOUND"))),
         currency = na_if(currency, "NOT_FOUND"))

problems(srn_wide)

srn_wide |>  select(company_name, year, revenues, currency, employees_total, ghg_scope1) |>  head(10)


nrow(srn_wide) == n_company_years
```

**Task A:** Which share of firm-years reports Scope 1, Scope 2 (market-based) and Scope 3 emissions?
Is "missing" here a firm decision or a data problem?
How would you find out?

```{r task_A}

scope_vars <- c("ghg_scope1","ghg_scope2_mkt","ghg_scope3")
srn_wide |>  summarise(n_firm_years=n(), across(all_of(scope_vars), ~ mean(!is.na(.x)), .names = "share_{.col}"))

```

# Part 4 · Merges: rebuilding a Ball & Brown (1968) sample

Ball and Brown (1968) needed **three data sources**: annual earnings (Compustat), monthly stock returns (CRSP) and announcement dates (Wall Street Journal).
Their inclusion criteria (p. 167):

1.  earnings data available on Compustat for each of the years 1946–1966,
2.  fiscal year ending December 31,
3.  price data available on CRSP for at least 100 months,
4.  Wall Street Journal announcement dates available.

Result: **261 firms**.
Today we build a modern version for 2010–2014 and count, step by step, how many firms survive each criterion (a **sample funnel**).

## Joins in dplyr

| Function | Keeps |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `left_join(x, y)` | all rows of `x`; `NA` where `y` has no match |
| `inner_join(x, y)` | only rows with a match in both |
| `anti_join(x, y)` | rows of `x` **without** a match in `y` — your best diagnostic tool |
| `full_join(x, y)` | all rows of both |

**Fan-out:** if a key appears twice in `y`, every matching row in `x` is duplicated.
Always compare the number of rows before and after a join.

### Chunk 4.1 · Step 1: Compustat — US firms, earnings available, December year-end

A small helper records firms and firm-years after every step (given — just run it):

```{r funnel_helper}
funnel <- tibble(step = character(), firms = integer(), firm_years = integer())
add_step <- function(funnel, step, data) {
  add_row(funnel, step = step, firms = n_distinct(data$gvkey), firm_years = nrow(data))
}
```

```{r chunk_4_1}

bb <- cs_indl
funnel <- add_step(funnel, "Compustat INDL, fiscal year known", bb)

bb <- bb |> filter(fic == "USA", curcd == "USD")
funnel <- add_step(funnel, "US firms reporting in USD", bb)

bb <- bb |> filter(!is.na(ib))
funnel <- add_step(funnel, "Earnings (ib) available", bb)

bb <- bb |> filter(month(datadate) == 12)
funnel <- add_step(funnel, "Fiscal year ends in December", bb)

funnel

```

### Chunk 4.2 · Step 2: the CRSP–Compustat link table

Compustat identifies **firms** (`gvkey`), CRSP identifies **securities** (`permno`).
The link table says which permno belongs to which gvkey — and **when** (`linkdt` to `linkenddt`).

```{r chunk_4_2}

link_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "linking_table.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |> 
  rename_with(tolower)

print(link_raw)

count(link_raw, linktype)
```

Standard choice: keep primary links (`linkprim` P or C) of the reliable types `LU` and `LC`.
An open-ended link has no end date (`E` or missing) — we set it to "today".

```{r chunk_4_2b}

link <- link_raw |> 
  filter(linktype %in% c("LU", "LC"), linkprim %in% c("P", "C")) |> 
  mutate(linkdt = as.Date(linkdt),
         linkenddt = as.Date(if_else(linkenddt == "E", "2099-12-31", linkenddt)),
         permno = as.numeric(lpermno)) |> 
  select(gvkey, permno, linkdt, linkenddt)


## How many permnos per gvkey (over all time)?
link |>  count(gvkey) |>  count(n, name = "n_gvkeys")




```

### Chunk 4.3 · Merge with a date condition

A plain join by `gvkey` attaches **every** link ever valid for that firm → fan-out.
We must keep only the link valid on the fiscal year-end date (`datadate`).

```{r chunk_4_3}
nrow(bb)

## Naive join: what happens to the number of rows?
naive <- bb |>  left_join(link, by = "gvkey", relationship = "many-to-many")

nrow(naive)

## Correct: keep only links valid on datadate
bb_linked <- bb |> 
  inner_join(link, by = join_by(gvkey, between(datadate, linkdt, linkenddt)))

nrow(bb_linked)

## Check the key again: one row per gvkey-fyear?
bb_linked |>  count(gvkey, fyear) |>  filter(n > 1) |>  nrow()

## Who got lost? anti_join shows firms without a valid link
lost <- bb |>  anti_join(bb_linked, by = c("gvkey", "fyear"))

nrow(lost)

funnel <- add_step(funnel, "Valid CRSP link at fiscal year-end", bb_linked)

```

### Chunk 4.4 · Step 3: CRSP returns — at least 60 months of returns

Ball and Brown required 100 months of price data.
Our CRSP extract covers 2009–2015 (84 months), so we require **60 months**.

```{r chunk_4_4}

msf_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "monthly_stock_file.csv")) |> 
  rename_with(tolower)

print(msf_raw)

## Key check: one row per permno and month?
msf_raw |> count(permno, mthcaldt) |> filter(n > 1) |>  nrow()

## Look at one duplicate: are the rows identical?
msf_raw |>  filter(permno == 10065, mthcaldt == as.Date("2009-02-27"))

```

Most of these duplicates are **exact copies** of the same row; in the others only the ticker differs (the firm changed its ticker that month).
Return and price are identical, so we can keep one row — but only after we checked that they really are identical.

```{r chunk_4_4b}

msf_raw |>  distinct() |>  count(permno, mthcaldt) |> filter(n>1) |> nrow()


msf <- msf_raw |> 
  select(permno, date = mthcaldt, ret = mthret, prc = mthprc) |> 
  distinct()

msf |>  distinct() |>  count(permno, date) |> filter(n>1) |> nrow()

summary(msf$ret)

## Tickers are not stable: one permno, several tickers

months_per_permno <- msf |> 
  filter(!is.na(ret)) |> 
  count(permno, name = "n_month")

bb_crsp <- bb_linked |> 
  inner_join(months_per_permno, by = "permno") |> 
  filter(n_month >= 60)

funnel <- add_step(funnel, "At least 60 monthly returns on CRSP", bb_crsp)

funnel
```

### Chunk 4.5 · Bonus: the Ball & Brown idea in five lines

Do firms with **earnings increases** have higher stock returns over the fiscal year than firms with earnings decreases?

```{r chunk_4_5}

annual_ret <- msf |> 
  filter(!is.na(ret)) |> 
  mutate(year = year(date)) |> 
  group_by(permno, year) |> 
  summarise(n = n(), ret_annual = prod(1 + ret) - 1, .groups = "drop") |> 
  filter(n == 12)

bb_result <- bb_crsp |> 
  arrange(gvkey, fyear) |> 
  group_by(gvkey) |> 
  mutate(earnings_up = ib > lag(ib)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(!is.na(earnings_up)) |> 
  inner_join(annual_ret, by = c("permno", "fyear"="year")) |> 
  mutate(abn_ret = ret_annual - mean(ret_annual), .by = fyear)

bb_result |> 
  group_by(earnings_up) |> 
  summarise(n = n(), mean_abn_ret = mean(abn_ret), median_abn_ret = median(abn_ret))

```

# Part 5 · Auditing extracted data: SRN vs. Compustat

SRN values are extracted from sustainability reports — partly by humans, partly by AI.
SRN's own quality snapshot reports that about **74%** of the reviewed values are correct.
Blankespoor, Croom and Grant (2026) classify investor questions with a machine-learning model that agrees with human coders in about **75%** of cases.
In both cases: generated data are useful, but they must be **verified**.

Here we use an independent source: **revenues** in Compustat Global.
Both should report the group's net revenues in millions of the reporting currency.

### Chunk 5.1 · Compustat Global

```{r chunk_5_1}
## Key check: one row per isin + fyear?
## Same story as in Compustat North America: INDL and FS formats ...
## ... and firms that changed their fiscal year-end (two datadates per fyear)


```

## Which SRN firm-years found no partner in Compustat Global?

# Part 6 · Bug hunt: an AI-written merge script

An **assertion** is a check that stops your code when something is not as expected:

```{r chunk_6_0, error=TRUE}
x <- c(1, 2, 3)
stopifnot(length(x) == 3)        # OK: nothing happens
stopifnot(all(x > 1))            # stops with an error message
```

Three assertions you can use in almost every merge:

- the key is unique: `stopifnot(!any(duplicated(data[c("gvkey", "fyear")])))`
- no rows were added by a join: `stopifnot(nrow(after) == nrow(before))`
- identifiers look right: `stopifnot(all(nchar(data$gvkey) == 6))`

The script below was written by an AI for the prompt *"Merge Compustat with CRSP returns and the SRN revenues. Count the firms in the final sample."* It runs — mostly.
**Find the bugs** (10 min by hand, then 10 min with an AI tool of your choice — code only, never the data).

### Chunk 6.1 · The AI-generated script

```{r chunk_6_1, error=TRUE}
## ---- AI-generated script ----

## (a) Compustat: read the data
comp <- read.csv(here("data", "compustat.csv"))
comp <- comp |> filter(!is.na(fyear))

## (b) Link Compustat to CRSP
comp_crsp <- comp |>
  mutate(gvkey = as.character(gvkey)) |>
  left_join(link, by = "gvkey", relationship = "many-to-many")

## (c) Number of firms with a CRSP link
cat("Firms with CRSP link:", n_distinct(comp_crsp$gvkey), "\n")

## (d) Average monthly return per firm
avg_ret <- msf_raw |>
  group_by(permno) |>
  summarise(mean_ret = mean(mthret))
cat("Firms with returns:", sum(!is.na(avg_ret$mean_ret)), "\n")

## (e) SRN revenues in wide format
srn_rev_wide <- srn_raw |>
  filter(field_slug %in% c("revenues", "employees_total")) |>
  select(company_name, year, field_slug, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = field_slug, values_from = value)

## (f) Revenue per employee
srn_rev_wide <- srn_rev_wide |>
  mutate(rev_per_emp = as.numeric(revenues) / as.numeric(employees_total))
summary(srn_rev_wide$rev_per_emp)
```
